references.text: Isaiah uses the image of water flowing from thirsty souls, where God promises to pour out water on the thirsty and streams upon the dry land, an image that Jesus fulfills as the source of living water.
Here those who thirst are invited to come to the water, a direct parallel to Jesus' invitation for whoever believes to drink from him and have living water flow from within.
Ezekiel's vision of water flowing from the temple threshold and giving life is a prophetic precursor to Jesus' words that living water will flow from those who believe.
Zechariah describes living water that will flow out from Jerusalem, an image that Jesus interprets as coming from the inner being of believers.
In his conversation with the Samaritan woman, Jesus presents himself as the source of living water that will become a spring within whoever drinks, a theme he expands on in this verse.
At the crucifixion, blood and water flow from Jesus' side, symbolizing that he is the source of the living water now flowing out to believers.
